skill.name: agent-tools
skill.description: Use the inference.sh CLI to discover and run cloud AI apps for images, videos, language models, search, audio, 3D, and social automation.
skill.summary: Run hosted AI apps through the inference.sh CLI from Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.
skill.author: tul-sh

security_audit.summary: The skill is useful but includes critical install guidance that pipes a remote script into a shell and documents dynamic remote binary downloads. Most API-key and markdown backtick detections are false positives, but external CLI calls, cloud data transfer, and X automation remain real risks. Publication should require safer installation guidance and clear approval gates for data uploads and public actions.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to sh.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-sh guidance with a pinned package, a downloaded script review step, and checksum or signature verification before execution.

remediation.issue: Manual install uses dynamic shell substitution to choose a binary URL.
remediation.suggestion: Provide explicit platform-specific download links, pinned versions, and signed release verification instead of deriving commands from a remote manifest.

remediation.issue: The CLI can upload prompts and files to external apps.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before infsh app run commands, especially when using local files or sensitive prompts.

remediation.issue: The skill documents public X automation actions.
remediation.suggestion: Require a confirmation step before any post, follow, like, retweet, or direct message command.

remediation.issue: Installer safety claims are not independently supported in the skill text.
remediation.suggestion: Link to source code, release signatures, checksum policy, and a concise list of local changes made by the installer.

content.user_title: Run Cloud AI Apps from the CLI
content.value_statement: Teams need one way to discover and run hosted AI models without managing GPUs. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through inference.sh CLI workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains CLI installation, login, and API key setup for inference.sh.
Lists, searches, filters, and inspects available inference.sh apps.
Runs apps with inline input or saved input files.
Generates sample input files for supported apps.
Tracks asynchronous tasks and retrieves app outputs.
Covers image, video, LLM, search, 3D, audio, and X workflows.
limitations: Requires an inference.sh account, credits, network access, and the infsh CLI.
Sends prompts, files, and task inputs to external inference.sh apps.
Does not validate third-party app safety, costs, output rights, or data handling.
Social media actions require explicit user approval and connected account permissions.

use_cases.title: Prototype media workflows
use_cases.description: Find image or video apps, create sample inputs, and run approved generation tasks.

use_cases.title: Compare model options
use_cases.description: Search available apps, inspect schemas, and test hosted LLM or multimodal models.

use_cases.title: Automate research tasks
use_cases.description: Use search and language apps to gather, summarize, and save research outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Find an app
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-tools to list inference.sh image apps. Recommend three options and explain the input each app needs.

prompt_templates.title: Run a sample task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-tools to create a sample input for falai/flux-dev-lora. Ask me before running it with my prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Track a long job
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-tools to run google/veo-3-1-fast without waiting. Check the task status until the result is ready.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a multi-app workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an inference.sh workflow that searches the web, summarizes results with an LLM, and saves outputs. Ask before each external call.

output_examples.input: Find image generation apps for product mockups.
output: Recommended three image apps with strengths and input needs.
Suggested generating a sample input before any run.
Flagged approval before sending prompts to the cloud.

output_examples.input: Create a short video from my approved prompt.
output: Prepared the app input and submitted a video generation task.
Returned the task identifier and checked progress.
Reported the final download link when the task completed.

output_examples.input: Search for recent AI product launches and summarize them.
output: Selected a search app and requested approval for the external query.
Collected search results and summarized key launches.
Saved the result summary when requested.

best_practices: Inspect app details and input schemas before running any task.
Ask for explicit approval before network calls, file uploads, or social posts.
Use sample inputs and version pinning for repeatable runs.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installer scripts to shell in unattended sessions.
Do not send secrets, private files, or regulated data as app input.
Do not automate public social media actions without human approval.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps an AI assistant use the inference.sh CLI to discover and run hosted AI apps.

faq.question: Does it require an account?
faq.answer: Yes. Most workflows require an inference.sh account, authentication, credits, and network access.

faq.question: Can it generate images and videos?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents image and video app discovery, sample input creation, task execution, and result retrieval.

faq.question: Can it call language models?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for Claude and other hosted models through OpenRouter and inference.sh apps.

faq.question: Is my data sent externally?
faq.answer: Yes. Prompts, input files, and task data are sent to inference.sh apps when you run commands.

faq.question: Can it post to X?
faq.answer: The skill documents X automation apps. Any public action should require explicit approval first.
